problem: Two frozen independent OC2 review findings: startup secondary report can mask primary; returned-frame/source relation omitted by reader.

findings.title: Startup failure reporting can replace the primary exception

requirement.text: recorder前startup失败也写原件；write失败不发布；finally导出不能掩盖原异常或丢prefix。
Primary recorded first; each secondary write/cleanup error separately persists with relation to primary; re-raise original primary.

findings.static_counterexample: A preregistration guard raises ValueError; the except block appends it, but _write_exclusive_v1(startup-failures.json) then raises OSError. The unprotected write exits before bare raise. The outer runner receives OSError and preserve() records OSError as PRIMARY. Original ValueError only survives in the older role-less preregistration row. The unchanged worker RuntimeError/ImportError/OSError catch can report BLOCKED_BY_ENV instead of the original guard ValueError/FAILED.
findings.impact: Wrong primary identity and terminal classification when startup evidence cannot be persisted; later reset-secondary coverage does not establish startup persistence safety.
findings.coverage_gap: Existing preregistration-write case permits startup-failures.json persistence. New secondary freeze/export cases begin after RESET and do not exercise this second failure.

findings.title: Historical current verification omits returned frame to source acquisition relation

requirement.text: cached identity缺失拒绝；原JSON/frame SHA+bytes重算完整event/frame joins，不信receipt true/PASS。

findings.writer_semantics: Writer finds the actual returned observation in self._frames and sets returned_acquisition_id=frame.acquisition_id; source_acquisition_id=frame.source_acquisition_id or frame.acquisition_id. A derived frame can have distinct returned/source IDs. Required relation: returned frame exists in saved allocation/frame originals and its original source relation equals current.source_acquisition_id, with corresponding event/interval. Equality of the two IDs is not assumed.
findings.static_counterexample: In existing valid originals, change only operational-originals.current.returned_acquisition_id to a non-existent acquisition string; recompute that file sha256 and bytes in receipt.original_files as the existing tamper test does. All event/frame/source originals, source_acquisition_id, token, sequence, D/S and age remain unchanged. Schema only requires the returned key; historical reader never accesses its value. Existing conditions therefore still reach original_integrity=VERIFIED and source_prefix_complete=True despite missing returned-frame identity.
findings.impact: Historical source-integrity claim omits a causal relationship explicitly recorded by the writer. Does not claim live/native authority is minted.
findings.coverage_gap: Existing allocation/pair/episode/reset/schema tamper cases never change returned_acquisition_id.

OC2-PR-01.root_cause: _prepare_source_v1 appends an unclassified preregistration failure then directly writes startup-failures.json inside except. A second write exception escapes before bare raise; runner only sees/relabels it PRIMARY.
changes: Add one private registry field on _LiveApplicationV1, preregistration_primary: tuple[BaseException, int] | None = None, for exact exception object and already allocated failure_id; this is internal one-shot handoff, not public authority.

In _prepare_source_v1 except, replace the legacy role-less append with _failure_row_v1(record, "preregistration", error, primary_id=None) before any report write. Store (error, row["failure_id"]) in that field.

Write startup-failures.json once via existing _failure_write_v1 with phase="startup_failure_persistence" and same primary_id. That helper marks durable evidence incomplete and records OSError as linked SECONDARY without throwing it over the primary.

On failed startup report write, try existing _persist_failure_stage_v1(record, record.output, primary_id=id) once as a new distinct append-only sidecar, not a retry/overwrite. Wrap this fallback so an unexpected fallback exception is recorded as SECONDARY with durable flag false and original error is still re-raised. Bare raise in the original except must execute; no new raised wrapper exception.

At first runner preserve(), consume and clear preregistration_primary if present. Reuse its original exception/traceback/id rather than adding a duplicate PRIMARY; if the currently caught error is a different object, retain it as linked SECONDARY. When no pending preregistration primary exists, keep the existing _failure_row allocation path. Subsequent cleanup remains the existing secondary path.

Preserve exclusive file semantics, source_called/once guards, failure_id uniqueness and all original error text/types/terminal classification. Do not retry startup report or modify old artifacts. Direct Task1 _prepare callers still receive the original exception and can inspect persisted sidecar or in-memory incomplete evidence.

tests.injection: Create app using existing application/cpu_components. Raise one captured ValueError("CPU preregistration primary") from the existing _new_prefix_backend_v1 raw CPU construction seam inside _prepare; wrap _write_exclusive_v1 to raise OSError("CPU startup report secondary") only for startup-failures.json and delegate all other writes. Do not patch validators/preserve/runner/reader/verdicts.
tests.direct: Activate using existing tests.test_operational_prefix_v1.activate; call _prepare_source_v1; require caught exception is the captured original object. Inspect one PRIMARY ValueError and linked SECONDARY OSError plus new stage sidecar/incomplete flag; startup writer called once; catalog unavailable and once-only guard stays. Direct activation is not worker dispatch, so do not require direct job terminal FAILED.
tests.worker: app.execute_once through real CPU worker: partial receipt primary remains ValueError, worker FAILED (not BLOCKED_BY_ENV), exactly one attempt, exactly one PRIMARY with all secondaries referencing id, runner-failure durable bytes preserve same primary, startup report write once, no initialize/observer/RESET/capture/planner/model and no catalog.
tests.RED: Both cases must FAIL on activated R79 because original reporting OSError masks ValueError; these are not pre-existing passing controls.

OC2-PR-02.root_cause: reader never accesses current.returned_acquisition_id; checking only source event/D/S/age leaves recorded returned-frame identity and source relation unaudited.
changes: Add a narrow pure helper _current_source_event_v1(current: dict[str, Any], frames: list[dict[str, Any]], captures: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any] near reader helpers. Any is only the existing heterogeneous JSON value contract; no cast or suppression.

Require current returned/source IDs to be nonempty str. Resolve exactly one saved returned frame by acquisition_id; compute its original_source = frame["source_acquisition_id"] or frame["acquisition_id"]. Require original_source equals current.source_acquisition_id; do not compare returned ID directly with source ID.

Resolve exactly one source frame and exactly one CAPTURE event for original_source. Require the source frame and returned frame interval_id equal operation-<source_event.operation_id>. Derived frames copy the original interval in VisualRawRecorderV3._record_transformed_observation, so distinct returned/source IDs can pass this relation.

Return the selected existing source event. In verify_operational_prefix_originals_v1 replace only the current source next(...) lookup with this helper call after existing full frame/manifest checks. Keep all following token/domain/sequence/episode/S/bracket/age logic, previous full denominator checks, persisted-frame comparisons, and unavailable live authority unchanged.

No schema change required: referential integrity belongs in reader where frames/events exist. Do not loosen allocation counts or enable new transformed-frame production/acceptance in the broader OC2 recipe. The helper permits a valid distinct-ID relationship; this alone is not a claim that a synthetic derived slab passes all existing full-reader recipe constraints.

tests.fixture: Each case creates its own new CPU valid originals using unchanged cpu_components/app.execute_once, then edits only this test-owned operational-originals.current.returned_acquisition_id and recomputes only that file receipt hash/bytes exactly as existing tamper tests do. No historical raw or old manifests are edited.
tests.missing_returned: Set returned ID to absent nonempty string; keep source_id/token/age/all frames unchanged.
tests.wrong_source_relation: Select an existing frame with an acquisition ID different from current.source_acquisition_id whose (source_acquisition_id or acquisition_id) is also different; set only returned ID to it. Do not assume all differing IDs are invalid.
tests.assertions: Reader must reject original_integrity/source_prefix_complete while live_authority remains UNAVAILABLE; install existing no-live-D/backend sentinels after original generation. Both previously pass incorrectly, so both RED failures are expected.
tests.control_execution: Post-fix GREEN only; helper does not exist in pre-fix source, so do not manufacture a RED from missing helper.
tests.control_data: Pure small JSON records: source frame acquisition source-1, source_acquisition_id None, interval operation-7; CAPTURE source-1 operation_id7. direct returned source-1; derived adds returned-1 with source_acquisition_id source-1 and same interval operation-7. Assert helper returns original capture event for both. This is relation-unit evidence, not a real source/derived transformation run.
